title: Compress a sealed vessel
hook: Change gas volume and predict ideal-gas pressure.
misconception: ideal-gas pressure doubles when gas volume doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply P = nRT/V to compare ideal-gas pressure when gas volume changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed quantity of ideal gas at fixed absolute temperature, P = nRT/V. When gas volume doubles, ideal-gas pressure becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model P = nRT/V; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed quantity of ideal gas at fixed absolute temperature, with a nonzero initial result. If gas volume triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on ideal-gas pressure?
recall.why: Apply P = nRT/V under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
